Senses.Explanation: A silver pellet is pictured as a small rounded ball that can be traded or kneaded into shape; the eight witnesses do not say whether it is solid silver, silver-colored, or a conventional named image. Nanquan Puyuan makes it the lower-priced side of a refused exchange between Chan instruction and scripture exposition, while Tian'an Sheng and Wuyi Yuanlai put an iron palm kneading one inside paired no-trace and craft images. In the early Nanquan encounter, a scripture lecturer offers to explain scripture if Nanquan explains Chan; Nanquan replies, ‘You must not trade a gold pellet for a silver pellet’ (不可將金彈子博銀彈子去). The turn structure places Nanquan's requested Chan explanation on the gold side and the lecturer's offered scripture exposition on the silver side. Zhengtang Bian's later verse on the case confirms that the comparison concerns valuation: ‘people know what is precious but do not know the price’ (世人知貴不知價). That establishes a local ranking in this public exchange, not a universal equation of gold with enlightenment or silver with lesser realization. The term's other family prevents that overreach. Tian'an Sheng and Wuyi Yuanlai both give the matched lines ‘where one hides, leave no traces: a gold needle embroiders a jade qilin; where there are no traces, do not hide: an iron palm kneads a silver pellet’ (藏身處沒蹤跡，金針繡出玉麒麟；沒蹤跡處莫藏身，鐵掌挪成銀彈子). Tian'an continues by reversing head and tail and saying that every device arrives and every teaching is fully displayed; Wuyi places the couplet in an end-of-retreat hall address and follows it with a challenge about an arrow passing through at a hundred paces. In these independent uses the silver pellet is handled as a compressed craft image, not as the inferior member of a gold-and-silver trade. The records do not state whether the imagined pellet is made of silver, merely silver-colored, or named by conventional comparison, so the displayed target identifies the whole image without asserting solid-silver construction.
Senses.Note: One lexical image covers the barter and kneading frames: both passages name a silver pellet or ball, while their local appraisals differ. They are deployments of the same object-image, not different referents. Four parallel lamp witnesses transmit Nanquan's barter form, one verse collection transmits the exchange verb ‘swap’ and adds Zhengtang Bian's no-headword comment, and three witnesses preserve the iron-palm line. Duplicate transmissions are inventoried in WORK.md but are not mechanically stored as separate depth padding. Three exact-headword anchors cover the independent encounter and two independent kneading speakers; the fourth stored occurrence is support only.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問坐主云。爾與我講經得麼對云。某甲與和尚講經。和尚須與某甲說禪始得。師云。不可將金彈子博銀彈子去。座主云。某甲不會。師云。汝道。空中一片雲。為復釘釘住。為復藤纜著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄) records Nanquan Puyuan asking a scripture lecturer whether he can lecture a scripture; when the lecturer offers scripture exposition in exchange for Chan instruction, Nanquan refuses to trade a gold pellet for a silver pellet. Nanquan's identity is confirmed by the same passage under his explicit heading in later lamp records.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頌曰。盤走珠𠔃珠走盤當機脫畧好生觀世人知貴不知價信手拈來也不雖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked-Pearl Compendium of Verses on Old Chan Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) appends a verse explicitly signed by Zhengtang Bian to Nanquan Puyuan's gold-for-silver pellet exchange. Zhengtang Bian says that people know what is precious but do not know the price. This no-headword support is separated from Nanquan's exact turn and does not buy silver-pellet depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 藏身處沒蹤跡，金針繡出玉麒麟；沒蹤跡處莫藏身，鐵掌挪成銀彈子。拈頭作尾、拈尾作頭，舉一機，機機頓赴；示一法，法法全彰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tian'an Sheng, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian'an Sheng (天岸昇禪師語錄), pairs a gold needle embroidering a jade qilin with an iron palm kneading a silver pellet, then speaks of reversing head and tail and fully displaying every device and teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只須藏身處沒蹤跡，金鍼繡出玉麒麟；沒蹤跡處莫藏身，鐵掌挪成銀彈子。諸昆仲！今日解制之辰，三年果滿，萬行週圓。且道：百步穿揚一箭作麼生透得過？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuyi Yuanlai, in the Essential Collection of the Recorded Sayings of Master Boshan Wuyi (博山無異大師語錄集要), places the gold-needle and iron-palm couplet in an end-of-retreat hall address and follows the silver pellet with a question about an arrow passing through at a hundred paces.
